meta.title: Host Syscall Behavior → MITRE ATT&CK Mapper
meta.description: Evidence-qualified candidate mappings from host syscall and endpoint telemetry to ATT&CK techniques.
meta.warning: A syscall or anomaly score alone does not prove a technique. Apply mappings only when required_events are observed and limitations are addressed.

required_events: ptrace against a process other than the caller's expected debugging target
process_vm_readv or corroborating remote-process memory access
limitations: ptrace can be used legitimately by debuggers; target-process and caller context are necessary.
The current eBPF watcher must capture process_vm_readv for the full requested signature.

required_events: OpenProcess access to lsass.exe with suspicious memory-read rights
MiniDumpWriteDump or equivalent LSASS memory-dump evidence
limitations: Requires Windows API or EDR telemetry; Linux eBPF syscall records do not observe these Windows APIs.

required_events: Registry value creation or modification under a Run/RunOnce or recognized startup location
Value data that launches an executable or script
limitations: RegSetValue without registry path and value data is insufficient.

required_events: init_module or finit_module loads an unexpected or untrusted module
Module identity, provenance, or privilege context supports suspiciousness
limitations: Module loading is a legitimate administrative action; syscall presence alone is not sufficient to label persistence.

syscall_attack_profiles.attack_type: Abuse of setuid/setgid for privilege escalation
required_events: setuid, setresuid, or setgid causes an unexpected privilege transition
Process identity and parent/child context indicate unauthorized elevation
limitations: A privilege-changing syscall is not inherently malicious; compare resulting identity and process context with expected behavior.

required_events: Rapid writes or file replacements across many files
Write/truncate/rename flags and corroborating content or file-change evidence
limitations: Rapid openat activity by itself is not evidence of encryption.
The current 128-D host vector does not encode write flags or file-content changes; do not fire this mapping from openat rate alone.
